meta.go_live_reference: Phased: Wave 1 (Stores) Q2, Wave 2 (Back Office) Q4

principles.statement: Training is built around what each role does, not generic system tours.
principles.implication: Curricula are assembled per learner group in the TNA stage; no one-size-fits-all courses.

principles.statement: Training lands close to each wave's go-live, when it will be used and remembered.
principles.implication: Delivery is scheduled per wave against go-live offsets, not one big-bang campaign.

principles.statement: Teach the critical path; reinforce the rest in the flow of work.
principles.implication: Formal seat time is kept short; in-app guidance and job aids carry the long tail.

principles.statement: Modular content is reused across business units, locations, and waves.
principles.implication: Core content is built centrally; local variants are thin overlays, not rebuilds.

principles.statement: Local trainers and champions carry and sustain delivery.
principles.implication: Train-the-trainer precedes every wave; champions own post-go-live reinforcement.

modality_strategy.rationale: Store staff are hard to release from the floor and turnover is high; task-level help at the moment of need beats classroom hours.
Back-office processes carry higher complexity and judgment; these roles can be scheduled and benefit from practice before go-live.

governance.owns: Strategy, TNA, curriculum design, reusable core content, delivery coordination, readiness gates
Content accuracy for their processes; validate role-to-curriculum mapping; approve readiness
Provide trainers and SMEs; release learners to attend; back-fill champions
Deliver and reinforce locally; surface adoption friction; sustain proficiency post-go-live

resourcing.core_team: Small core team — training lead plus instructional designers; exact sizing is a TNA/curriculum-stage output.
resourcing.multipliers: Train-the-trainer model; store super-users and back-office champions deliver at scale and reinforce locally.
resourcing.vendor_stance: Vendor acceptable for content-development surge and LMS administration; process knowledge and ownership stay in-house.

build_vs_buy.rationale: Acme's corporate LMS already reaches both workforce types.
No tool licensed yet; decision needed before content development starts — see open questions.
Off-the-shelf vendor content covers basic navigation; custom effort goes to role/process content.
Acme-specific processes; accuracy owned by business process owners.

measurement.approach: Kirkpatrick framing: L1 reaction, L2 competency checks for transactional roles, L3 behavior via adoption and in-app usage, L4 process outcomes returning to baseline. Completion and competency thresholds feed the go/no-go readiness gate per wave; hypercare metrics decide when reinforcement tapers.
links: Detailed L1–L4 measurement plan: training-rollout-builder output

phasing.description: Certify local trainers and champions on the wave's core content.
Confirm content, trainers, and learners are ready; low-readiness groups trigger targeted intervention.
Deliver by role, close to that wave's go-live, per the modality strategy.
In-app guidance, floor support by champions, and refreshers until support metrics stabilize.

risks.risk: Frontline learners cannot be released from the floor during the holiday trading peak.
risks.mitigation: Microlearning and in-app guidance minimize classroom time; wave schedule avoids peak weeks.

risks.risk: Business trainers are nominated but not back-filled, so delivery capacity collapses at scale.
risks.mitigation: Back-fill commitment secured as part of the governance model before train-the-trainer begins.

risks.risk: Content is built before design is confirmed, forcing rework.
risks.mitigation: Content development gated on process-design sign-off by business process owners.

assumptions: A sandbox environment is available at least 60 days before each wave's go-live.
The existing corporate LMS can host and track all planned content types.
The change network (champions) is stood up before Wave 1 train-the-trainer.

open_questions.question: Which in-app guidance / digital adoption platform will be licensed, if any?
What is the training budget envelope, and does it cover vendor content-development surge?
open_questions.needed_by: Before the TNA is sized into a curriculum

open_questions.question: Are competency sign-offs required (vs. completion only) for transactional roles at the readiness gate?
open_questions.needed_by: Before the measurement plan is detailed
